title: The eastern hedge
hookLine: Tao Yuanming picks chrysanthemums by the hedge and sees the southern mountain (Drinking Wine 5)
tomorrow: a hermit writes poems on rocks. who's meant to read them?

lines: I'LL RELAX ONCE I GET AWAY.
cards: Plenty of people say they'll finally relax once they get away: the cabin, the beach, the retreat.
Tao Yuanming stayed put, and wrote a puzzle about it: I built my hut where people live, yet I hear no noise of carts and horses. Same road, same traffic. He even asks himself: how can that be?
And answers: when the heart is far away, the place becomes remote on its own.

teach.b: Then he shows you how it works. Picking chrysanthemums by the eastern hedge, at ease, I see the southern mountain. The mountain air is lovely at sunset; birds fly home together.
In this there's a true meaning. I want to explain it, and I've already forgotten the words. Two puzzles, one answer.
First: the quiet came from where his heart was, not where his hut was.

Tradition says he quit an official post rather than bow to a visiting inspector for a salary of rice, and went home to farm; but this poem doesn't tell you to flee to the hills. He stayed where people live.

teach.h: THE FISH TRAP: FORGET THE WORDS.
teach.b: That's the Zhuangzi, the Daoist classic: a fish trap is for catching fish; once you have the fish, you forget the trap.

teach.h: LOOK UP FROM A SMALL TASK.
teach.b: Words are for meaning; once you have the meaning, you can forget the words. So the teaching, as Daoist readers hear it: the way isn't found by explaining it, and stillness isn't a place you can buy.
He looks up from a small task, flowers in his hand, and the mountain is simply there.

how: Daoist teaching values a quiet heart over a quiet place, and the Zhuangzi's fish trap reminds readers that words point past themselves. Tao Yuanming's Drinking Wine 5 is read as that teaching lived on a small farm.

o: a border wall built against raiders coming from the east
the hedge where Tao Yuanming picked flowers and saw the mountain
a garden where the monks grew tea for the temple

games.q: the hut, the hedge, the trap: tap the pairs.
p: built his hut where people live
once you have the fish, forget it

s: Tao Yuanming moved deep into the mountains to escape people
he says he built his hut where people live. the quiet came from the heart.
the poem ends by saying he has forgotten the words
an echo of the Zhuangzi: once you have the meaning, forget the words.
the Zhuangzi's fish trap is advice about fishing
it's about words: once the meaning is caught, the words can go.

games.q: your brother says he can only meditate on retreat, never at home. what fits Tao Yuanming?
o: the heart far off makes any place remote; try it at home.
he's right; the poet quit his job and left the town.
stillness needs total silence, so buy better headphones.
games.why: Tao Yuanming lived where people live and heard no carts: when the heart is far, the place grows remote.

practice: Do one small task with your hands: fold something, straighten a cup, line up a pen. Then look up, without planning to, and find the farthest thing you can see: a roofline, a tree, the far wall.
Rest your eyes there, and leave it unexplained.

wordCard.voice: The eastern hedge: where Tao Yuanming picked flowers and, looking up, saw the southern mountain.

orig.s: 采菊東籬下 悠然見南山
orig.say: tsai jyoo dong lee shyah, yoh rahn jyen nahn shahn
orig.note: Chinese: picking chrysanthemums by the eastern hedge, at ease I see the southern mountain. Tao Yuanming, Drinking Wine 5.

carryVoice: Keep this: the southern mountain, there all along when you look up. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Tao Yuanming, Drinking Wine, poem 5 (Yin jiu, 5)
